title: Duality of Shortfall Aversion
abstract: arXiv:2610.32350v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Shortfall aversion describes a form of consumption habit formation in which an individual's utility depends on consumption relative to the historical consumption peak. This study develops a duality framework for a broad class of utility functions, with and without discounting, avoiding the need for determining the local optimality required by the HJB approaches commonly adopted in the literature. We show that shortfall aversion can instead be incorporated directly into the dual problem through a singular-control mechanism characterized by a variational inequality. Furthermore, we establish that the resulting value function strictly dominates those obtained in the existing literature while remaining attainable under an admissible optimal control. translated_abstract: 缺口厌恶描述了消费习惯形成的一种形式，即个体的效用取决于消费相对于历史消费峰值的水平。本研究为一大类效用函数（包括含贴现与不含贴现的情形）构建了对偶框架，从而避免了文献中常用的 HJB（Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman）方法所必需的局部最优性判定。我们证明，缺口厌恶可以通过一种由变分不等式刻画的奇异控制机制，直接纳入对偶问题之中。此外，我们证明了由此得到的价值函数严格占优于现有文献中的结果，同时在可容许的最优控制下仍然可以实现。我们进一步表明，现有解的次优性源于其对消费峰值更新的短视处理，而我们的对偶方法则扩大了可容许解类的范围（原文此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出一种对偶框架，通过由变分不等式刻画的奇异控制机制将缺口厌恶直接纳入对偶问题，所得价值函数严格优于且可实现，超越了现有文献中因对消费峰值更新短视处理而导致的次优解。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a duality framework that incorporates shortfall aversion directly into the dual problem via a singular-control mechanism characterized by a variational inequality, yielding a value function that strictly dominates the suboptimal solutions in the existing literature—which stem from the myopic treatment of consumption-peak updates—while remaining attainable under an admissible optimal control.
